feedback: The RM faithfully encodes the task G(blocker_moved -> F has_door_key) (the Response rule the level notes reference). u1 is exactly the all-obligations-discharged state: it is entered only on has_door_key, which discharges the obligation active from step 1 (blocker_moved is true at the first step), and it is left only when blocker_moved & !has_door_key recurs, i.e., the key is dropped while the ball is clear. That regression is explicit and penalised (-0.5), and the repair u2 -> u1 on re-pickup is rewarded (+0.2), so the automaton can leave its final state, which this response-style task requires. The accepting set is exact: satisfying traces end in u1, while any trace ending in u0 (key never acquired) or u2 (drop never repaired) violates the property, so FINAL_STATES: u1 is declared, nonempty, and accepting for the task. Using the persistent condition pair blocker_moved & !has_door_key instead of the key_lost event is the semantically correct choice: key_lost misses drops made while the door is open, which still create an obligation while the ball is out of the way, whereas the condition pair catches them; conversely, a door-closed drop with the ball sitting in front of the door correctly draws no penalty until blocker_moved turns true again, matching the per-moment obligation. Persistent/event distinctions are handled correctly (no latching of u1 on first pickup; blocker_moved treated as revertible). Irrelevant propositions (door_open, target_picked_up, key_lost) are covered by per-state else self-loops; guards are predicate-only; else is ordered last in each state block; all three states are reachable (key is acquirable without touching the ball, drops and re-pickups are feasible). Format matches the paper template (REWARD_MACHINE/STATES/INITIAL_STATE/FINAL_STATES/TRANSITION_FUNCTION/REWARD_FUNCTION). Rewards are dense enough for this task, bounded, and farming-proof: the first pickup is +1.0, every +0.2 repair is preceded by a -0.5 in the same cycle (net -0.3), total return is capped at 1.0, and the optimal policy under the RM (acquire the key and keep it) ends in the final state and satisfies the task. Review only; no rewrite performed.

feedback:
All five environment-declared propositions are implemented with no extras, no missing predicates, no imports, no mutations, and valid Python.

blocker_moved: The candidate scans the grid for a door cell (guarded by x > 0) and checks whether the cell to its left, (dx-1, dy), holds a ball. Since there is exactly one door and the start room is on the left, this is equivalent to the documented expression `not any(c is not None and c.type == "ball" for c in [env.grid.get(dx-1, dy)])`. A carried ball is not on the grid, so it counts as moved; dropping the ball back on the front cell makes it false again; at the first step no ball is at (dx-1, dy), so it is true. Condition (not latch) semantics preserved; it is a pure current-state read.

has_door_key: Matches the documented expression exactly (carrying a key whose color equals some door's color).

door_open: Matches the documented expression exactly (any door with is_open), so it reverts if the door were ever toggled shut.

target_picked_up: Matches the documented expression exactly (carrying a box whose color matches the mission string), with no fixed-color assumption.

key_lost: Correct event semantics. It reads env.episode_memory["previous_valuation"] read-only, requires prev has_door_key true, recomputes K and D inline (character-for-character identical to the has_door_key and door_open bodies) and requires both false now. At the first step the previous valuation has has_door_key false, so the event is false; it fires only on the single step after the key is dropped while the door is closed, not lingering. The truthiness guard on previous_valuation is harmless given the documented complete valuation and only prevents a KeyError-style failure.

No function mutates the environment or episode memory; all reads (env.carrying, env.mission, env.grid.get, env.width/height, episode_memory) are within the documented API, empty cells are guarded with `cell is not None` before attribute access, and grid scans stay within 0 <= x < env.width, 0 <= y < env.height (with x > 0 additionally guarding the x-1 lookup). Persistent propositions read only current state; only the declared event touches the previous valuation. Constraint compatibility holds (key_lost excludes has_door_key and door_open by construction; blocker_moved true from step 1). Accepted.
